title: Founding of Carthage
summary: By tradition, Phoenician settlers from Tyre founded Carthage on the coast of North Africa in 814 BCE. Later accounts name Elissa, a Tyrian princess better known as Dido, as the founder, but the story is legendary. Carthage began as a minor port and was a major centre of trade by the 4th century BCE.

uncertainty.note: 814 BCE is the traditional date (astronomical -813). World History Encyclopedia says the founder's historicity has been challenged but the founding dates to about this time; the account is legendary.

as_recorded.value: founded c. 814 BCE by the legendary Phoenician queen Dido
according to tradition, Carthage was founded in 814 BCE by a Phoenician princess named Elissa

where.historical_name: Carthage, a colony of Tyre on the North African coast; the settlement was on the hill later called Byrsa

importance.justification: Origin of the city that became a major Mediterranean trading centre and Rome's rival.

sources.title: Pompeius Trogus on the Founding of Carthage
sources.author: Livius.org

beats.caption: Tradition has Elissa of Tyre land on the African coast, win ground by the ox-hide trick, and found the city.
The minor port that served Phoenician traders has become a major centre of trade.

reviewer_note: Least sure: the date is traditional and the founder legendary; the record marks it contested. Livius adds that Carthage was founded seventy-two years before Rome. 813 vs 814 BCE variants (Timaeus) were not on the opened pages. Pleiades point is a representative site point.
